items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: She joined Ventura after we left... she said that he had her write down all the syllables... I said, 'Oh Ruth, that’s terrible to have to do that.'

ctx.x: But in the beginning we had some pretty funny ones I must admit. Like we did a tune of Roy’s called “Euphoria” which was based on the changes of “S’Wonderful.” And it was pretty [scats]. I mean we had some [scats] and now it sounds dumb to us. But I remember one time we were working in a club in San Francisco and some guy who was going to college there came up and he was sitting there writing most every night and I thought what the heck is he doing? And he was making a survey on how many times we sang certain…
I never count how much you sing them. But here’s a funny one. We left Ventura at the end of 1949. Then Ruth Price, who runs the Jazz Bakery out in Los Angeles and is doing © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

very well with it, is also a singer. She joined Ventura after we left, and she said that he had her write down all the syllables on long butcher paper, just sheets of it. And she said she would have it hanging on the walls anywhere she could see it so she could do these charts the same way. And I said, “Oh Ruth, that’s terrible to have to do that. Why don’t you just make up your own?” She says, “no, he wanted just like it was on the original.
